evidence: chapter-15.md: "⌈344/35⌉ = 10 hosts at 40 rps, bounded below by the ~7-host prefill requirement — prefill compute then binds" inside a sentence whose scope note says "under ... the 35% MFU assumption". evidence: chapter-26.md: "because the 50 ms retrieval term is part of the baseline, the headline −44% is measured against the full 450 ms path (a queue-inflated baseline - 320 + 80 + 50 = 450 - against a queue-drained miss - 120 + 80 + 50 = 250, step 2); excluding that term entirely (a 400 ms baseline) would report (400 − 250) / 400 = 37.5% instead." chapter-24.md: "samples 1,000 retrievals per cycle (n ≈ 1,000 sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; 0.001 resolution)". Recomputed: rule of three — 0 events in n=1,000 gives a 95% upper bound of 3/1,000 = 0.003 = exactly the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; the finding's own number P(X=0|λ=3) = e⁻³ = 0.0498 ✓ confirms the 95% property. n = 1,000 IS sized for the target as a pass/fail acceptance test (certify only on 0 events), and 1 event = 0.001 resolution ✓; the finding's Wilson CI [0.0010, 0.00878] (recomputed) describes x=3, i.e. a failed cycle, not the design basis.

evidence: chapter-21.md: "The canonical service does ~288,000 requests/workday (10 rps × 8 h × 3,600 s; ~6.24M/month — Ch 4's 8-h × 260-workday calendar basis...)". Recomputed: 10×8×3,600 = 288,000/day ✓; 288,000 × 260 = 74,880,000 per YEAR; 74,880,000 ÷ 12 = 6,240,000/month exactly. chapter-04.md states the basis explicitly: "6,240,000 — the 260-workday year averaged to a month". The finding multiplied the 260-workday year against a monthly figure (74.9M is yearly, not monthly); 10 rps and 6.24M/month are consistent, so the P0 arithmetic-incompatibility claim fails.
